provenance.method: original bounded training scenarios; technique categories and links reference public standards
provenance.accuracy_note: This learning set covers 15 MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise tactics, not every sub-technique. Always consult the linked current source.

scenarios.title: Unexpected public asset discovery
scenarios.brief: In a fictional enterprise, an internet-facing sandbox application appears in an asset inventory report without an owner.
controls: Maintain an owner-backed external asset inventory
Classify data and remove unnecessary public exposure
Review change and publication records
scenarios.critic: A public service is not automatically a compromise; establish ownership and scope before risk scoring.
scenarios.question: What should the analyst do first?
choices: Attempt access against the unfamiliar service
Validate ownership and business need, then classify exposure
Assume the host is hostile and publish its address
scenarios.rationale: Inventory and ownership validation establish scope and reduce false assumptions.

scenarios.title: Lookalike domain awareness
scenarios.brief: A synthetic brand-protection feed reports a newly registered lookalike domain; its owner and intent are unknown.
controls: Review authorized brand-protection intelligence
Improve mail-domain authentication and user reporting
Track suspicious indicators with uncertainty labels
scenarios.critic: String similarity and a certificate are indicators, not proof of malicious intent.
scenarios.question: Which evidence standard fits?
choices: Classify as confirmed compromise
Collect corroborating public evidence and label as unverified
Launch traffic against the domain
scenarios.rationale: Corroborate signals and preserve confidence before escalation.

scenarios.title: Suspicious sign-in lure
scenarios.brief: A fictional employee reports an email requesting an urgent MFA approval for an unrecognized sign-in.
controls: Teach independent verification of sign-in prompts
Use phishing-resistant authentication where appropriate
Revoke compromised sessions if confirmed
scenarios.critic: Do not assume credential theft from one unapproved MFA push; correlate authentication events.
scenarios.question: What is the safe immediate action?
choices: Approve the request to stop notifications
Report the lure and deny unexpected MFA prompts
Send your password to helpdesk by email
scenarios.rationale: User reporting and denying unfamiliar approvals avoid authorizing unwanted access.

scenarios.title: Unexpected script process
scenarios.brief: An authorized test laptop logs a script engine launched from a temporary directory during a simulation.
controls: Correlate process lineage and signed-file evidence
Check endpoint policy and approved software inventory
Escalate a documented suspicious execution for triage
scenarios.critic: A script process alone cannot prove malicious execution; validate origin and approved workflows.
scenarios.question: Which triage artifact is most useful?
choices: Process ancestry and approved-software context
A random unrelated account password
Unattributed social-media speculation
scenarios.rationale: Process lineage and allowlisting context help distinguish administrative work from suspicious activity.

scenarios.title: Unplanned startup entry
scenarios.brief: A test image receives an unexpected startup entry outside the approved configuration baseline.
controls: Audit startup mechanisms against a change baseline
Check software signing and owner approval
Document rollback under approved change procedures
scenarios.critic: Updates and vendor installers also create startup entries; validate provenance.
scenarios.question: What best prevents recurring drift?
choices: Disable audit logs
Baseline startup configurations and alert on unauthorized changes
Ignore new entries for 90 days
scenarios.rationale: Baseline and change approval make unauthorized persistence visible without blanket assumptions.

scenarios.title: Unreviewed privileged role grant
scenarios.brief: A synthetic identity record shows a privileged cloud role grant that lacks a matching approval ticket.
controls: Apply just-in-time and least-privilege access
Require approval and review logs for role grants
Remove unauthorized privileges through change-controlled response
scenarios.critic: Absence of an approval ticket may indicate lagging paperwork; validate owner before attribution.
scenarios.question: Which control most directly limits this risk?
choices: Permanent standing admin access for everyone
Least privilege with audited role elevation
Turn off access reviews
scenarios.rationale: Controlled elevation and auditability reduce privileged access exposure.

scenarios.title: Unexpected telemetry blind spot
scenarios.brief: A fictional fleet-health service reports a silent host sensor while network monitoring still sees the device online.
controls: Alert on missing and degraded telemetry
Use independent sensor-health evidence
Investigate planned maintenance and logging configuration
scenarios.critic: Sensor outage is not evidence of intentional hiding unless corroborated.
scenarios.question: What evidence should be checked first?
choices: Only the last application message
Sensor health and maintenance/change history
A vulnerability scanner against unrelated networks
scenarios.rationale: Independent health and maintenance records help isolate telemetry failures.

scenarios.title: Disabled protective control
scenarios.brief: In a sandbox, a protection agent is disabled after an unexplained configuration change.
controls: Alert on security-control state changes
Protect monitoring configurations from unauthorized edits
Restore approved baselines after operator review
scenarios.critic: Maintenance and compatibility incidents may disable controls legitimately; confirm change ownership.
scenarios.question: Which response is most appropriate?
choices: Silently delete all configuration evidence
Confirm authorization, preserve logs, and restore a known-good policy
Disable monitoring on other systems
scenarios.rationale: Preserving evidence and controlled restoration address the incident without erasing context.

scenarios.title: Unusual authentication failures
scenarios.brief: Synthetic identity logs show many unsuccessful sign-ins to a lab-only account followed by one success.
controls: Use phishing-resistant MFA and risk-based authentication
Correlate session, device, and location changes
Review and terminate suspicious sessions when substantiated
scenarios.critic: A failed-login spike could be user error or testing; correlate activity before declaring takeover.
scenarios.question: Which step strengthens the assessment?
choices: Correlate successful session with MFA and device provenance
Publish the credential for others to test
Suppress authentication logs
scenarios.rationale: Session provenance can distinguish anomalous access from normal recovery.

scenarios.title: Unusual directory enumeration
scenarios.brief: A simulated audit observes a service account reading far more directory objects than normal.
controls: Apply minimal directory read permissions
Use per-identity behavior baselines
Verify approved discovery and inventory jobs
scenarios.critic: An approved inventory sync might be expected; compare schedule and ownership.
scenarios.question: How should this be handled?
choices: Delete the service account immediately with no review
Compare against job schedule and permissions, then triage anomalies
Give the service account global admin
scenarios.rationale: Authorized discovery may produce spikes; context supports proportional action.

scenarios.title: Unexpected internal connection pattern
scenarios.brief: A fictional segmented lab records remote-session attempts between two systems that normally do not communicate.
controls: Apply zero-trust segmentation rules
Audit remote administration paths
Validate lateral connections against approved workflows
scenarios.critic: Network migration can generate atypical flows; check deployment status before attribution.
scenarios.question: Which defensive design best limits movement?
choices: Open all internal ports to every host
Least-privilege segmentation with remote-access logging
Turn off east-west network logs
scenarios.rationale: Segmentation and visibility reduce unauthorized cross-system traversal.

scenarios.title: Abnormal archive creation
scenarios.brief: An approved test account generates a large archive from a restricted lab directory outside a documented job.
controls: Classify and govern sensitive data locations
Monitor unusual bulk access and archive events
Use role-based access with evidence retention
scenarios.critic: Backups can look like large collections; verify schedule and authorization.
scenarios.question: Which signal is key for triage?
choices: Data classification and approved job context
Screen resolution of the workstation
Public IPs of unrelated organizations
scenarios.rationale: Classification and workload approvals establish whether collection was authorized.

scenarios.title: Regular uncommon DNS lookups
scenarios.brief: A mock resolver sees highly regular lookups to a rarely used domain from one lab host.
controls: Correlate DNS timing with application inventory
Establish expected outbound-domain policy
Review endpoint and resolver evidence jointly
scenarios.critic: Scheduled update checks often look periodic; timing is not sufficient proof.
scenarios.question: What is a grounded next step?
choices: Correlate resolver logs with known installed software
Block all DNS everywhere permanently
Claim confirmed command-and-control from timing alone
scenarios.rationale: Process and software context distinguish expected periodic lookups from unexplained traffic.

scenarios.title: Unexpected outbound upload
scenarios.brief: Synthetic network telemetry flags an unusual upload volume from a test workstation to an unclassified destination.
controls: Classify authorized egress destinations
Use privacy-aware network and DLP signals
Preserve evidence and follow incident escalation policy
scenarios.critic: Legitimate media exports and backups can be large; validate user intent and destination.
scenarios.question: What should be established before concluding exfiltration?
choices: Destination authorization, data category and related change records
Only the volume in bytes
Whether unrelated social posts mention the company
scenarios.rationale: Flow size alone cannot determine the purpose or classification of transferred information.

scenarios.title: Unexpected backup retention change
scenarios.brief: A resilience exercise injects a fictional backup-policy change reducing retention from 30 days to 0.
controls: Protect immutable or isolated recovery copies
Require dual approval for retention policy changes
Verify restoration through periodic recovery exercises
scenarios.critic: A configuration diff is not proof of actual data destruction; test restore availability before impact claims.
scenarios.question: Which control best preserves recoverability?
choices: Disable all recovery testing
Maintain protected backups and test restoration
Keep the only backup on the same device
scenarios.rationale: Protected, tested recovery paths reduce the impact of destructive changes.
